seoTitle: How to Issue a Refund on eBay as a Seller
metaDescription: Need to refund a buyer on eBay? Learn how to send a full or partial refund from your Orders page and calculate the exact amount correctly.
intro: Whether a return request comes in, an item goes missing, or a buyer is simply unhappy, issuing a refund on eBay as a seller starts from the same place every time: the order itself. This guide walks through finding the Send refund option on a delivered order, using the refund calculator to get the amount right — including partial and order-level refunds — and where to go for policy guidance if a claim looks off. It's aimed at sellers who want to handle refunds correctly without guessing at the process.

steps.heading: Find the order and open Send refund
steps.body: From your Orders list, each delivered item shows a "View payment details" dropdown next to it. Opening that dropdown reveals four options: Contact buyer, Sell similar, Send refund, and Add note. Send refund is the one that starts the actual process — there's no separate refund page to hunt for elsewhere, it lives directly on the order.

image.caption: The order dropdown menu on a delivered item, with Send refund sitting between Contact buyer and Add note.

steps.heading: Decide between a full and a partial refund
steps.body: Before you click Send refund, decide what the buyer is actually owed. A full refund makes sense for a lost item, a wrong item, or a return you're accepting outright. A partial refund fits situations like a minor defect the buyer is keeping the item despite, or a shipping cost you're not refunding while still returning the item price. Having this decided up front makes the next screen faster, since it's asking for exact numbers rather than a simple yes/no.

steps.heading: Calculate the refund amount
steps.body: The Calculate refund amount screen lists each item on the order with its Paid amount next to an editable Refund field, defaulting to the full paid amount. Below the item list, an Order level refund field lets you add an extra amount that gets distributed across the items in the order — useful for refunding a portion of shipping or a bundled discount without editing each line item separately. The Total at the bottom updates live as you adjust either field, so you can confirm the number matches what you intend to send before moving on.

image.caption: The Calculate refund amount screen: Paid and Refund columns per item, an Order level refund field, and a running Total.

steps.heading: Review and submit the refund
steps.body: Once the numbers look right, click Review Refund. eBay shows you a final summary of exactly what's being sent and to whom before anything moves, giving you one last chance to catch a typo in the amount. Confirm from there to actually send it — Cancel is available on the same screen if something doesn't match what you intended.

steps.heading: Track where the funds land
steps.body: After a refund is sent, it's deducted from your available balance and returned to the buyer's original payment method, whether that's a card charged through eBay's payment system or a linked PayPal account on older orders. Processing time on the buyer's end typically runs a few business days, and you can revisit the same order's payment details to confirm the refund shows as processed rather than pending.

steps.heading: Use eBay's help resources when a claim looks off
steps.body: Not every refund request should be approved automatically. eBay's Customer Service search lets you look up specific policy questions — searching something like "refunding buyer" surfaces suggested articles such as returning an item for a refund or getting help with an item that hasn't arrived. If a claim seems inconsistent with the order details, checking the relevant policy article before you act protects you if the buyer escalates to the resolution center afterward.

image.caption: eBay's Customer Service search, with "refunding bu..." typed in and suggested help articles appearing below.

steps.heading: Keep your response fast to protect your seller rating
steps.body: Refund speed factors directly into eBay's seller performance metrics, so a legitimate request handled within a day or two does far less damage to your standing than one left open for a week. If a return has already been approved through the resolution center rather than started by you, eBay can process that refund automatically once the returned item is confirmed, so you don't always need to repeat the manual Send refund steps above.

faq.question: Can I issue a partial refund on eBay?
faq.answer: Yes — on the Calculate refund amount screen you can edit the Refund field for individual items, or use the Order level refund field to distribute an extra amount across the order instead of refunding the full paid price.

faq.question: How long does an eBay refund take to process?
faq.answer: It typically takes a few business days to reach the buyer's original payment method. You can check an order's payment details afterward to see whether the refund shows as processed or still pending.

faq.question: Does eBay ever issue refunds automatically?
faq.answer: Yes — if a return has already been approved through the resolution center, eBay can process the refund automatically once the returned item is confirmed, without you needing to use Send refund manually.

faq.question: Will refunding buyers affect my seller rating?
faq.answer: Handling legitimate refunds quickly, ideally within a day or two of the request, protects your seller performance metrics far more than delaying — slow response time counts against you more than the refund itself.

faq.question: What should I do if I suspect a fraudulent refund claim?
faq.answer: Search eBay's Customer Service help center for the relevant policy before approving — it surfaces specific guidance like returning an item for a refund or handling an item that hasn't arrived, which can clarify whether the claim holds up.
